instruction: Conceive new original identities from the locked architecture; do not reuse the prior A-Mail prompts or boards.

prompts.objective: Creative challenge 01: establish enduring authority. Conceive the identity as a serious, independent standard people could still trust in twenty years. Lead with exceptional typographic craft and a simple original mark. Develop your own visual metaphor and restrained palette. Make the board feel unusually assured, not corporate or bureaucratic.
prompts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Asset type: a polished, large landscape brand identity concept board for foundational open internet infrastructure.
Primary request: Conceive an ORIGINAL visual identity from a blank page. This is a new brand exploration, not a redesign of an old image. Invent the visual concept, symbol, typography pairing, palette and layout yourself from the architecture below. Make thoughtful design decisions, not a generic SaaS template. No reference images are supplied or to be used.

LOCKED NAMING ARCHITECTURE:
The umbrella open project is spelled exactly "MailSchema" (capital M and S).
Its first specification is spelled exactly "Mail Action Protocol". Its acronym is exactly "MAP".
It is NOT Mail Agent Protocol or Model Email Protocol. Never print those names.
MailSchema houses related specifications, shared interaction types and an implementation registry. MAP describes available service actions in email, authorized requests and explicit outcomes. Agents are first in the positioning; people retain control and have a normal readable email path. Implementations remain vendor-neutral; no single product is required for compatibility.
This is foundational infrastructure: credible enough for a technical specification and memorable enough to spread among developers.

EXACT SHORT COPY AVAILABLE:
"MailSchema"
"Open standards for agent interactions through email."
"Mail Action Protocol"
"MAP"
"0.1 — Draft"
"Email agents can act on."
"Shared types. Authorized requests. Clear outcomes."
"Types"
"Registry"
"Specification"
"Content Review"
"Services · Clients · Connectors"
"Review revision 4"
"Request changes"
"Approve revision 4"

BOARD CONTENT:
Show a powerful primary MailSchema wordmark and an original scalable symbol, including a small monochrome application; a subordinate MAP / Mail Action Protocol specification lockup that feels related; typography and color samples; a generous homepage hero concept; a compact specification-reader treatment; small Types and Registry applications; and a concrete email-review card with the exact revision 4 actions above. These applications should prove a cohesive identity, not imitate a full working dashboard. Give the important names and hierarchy ample space and use only short readable UI text. Clearly mark the specification Draft. Do not imply approval sends a campaign.
No fake adoption counts, partner logos, certification seals, standards-body endorsement, invented organization names or long lorem ipsum paragraphs.
Choose a fresh aesthetic and a high-quality composition with strong typography, disciplined spacing, confident negative space and a genuinely distinctive mark. Avoid @-sign/envelope/postal logos, bracket-and-bridge marks, geographical maps or compasses, AI brains/sparkles and glossy 3D blobs. Do not default to the usual ivory/cobalt, cream/vermilion or forest/lime brand-board palette.
Output one finished identity board, not a written explanation. Render MailSchema and Mail Action Protocol accurately.

Creative challenge 01: establish enduring authority. Conceive the identity as a serious, independent standard people could still trust in twenty years. Lead with exceptional typographic craft and a simple original mark. Develop your own visual metaphor and restrained palette. Make the board feel unusually assured, not corporate or bureaucratic.
Label the board discreetly "Direction 01".

prompts.objective: Creative challenge 02: make interoperability tangible. Conceive an original visual system in which different participants can understand a shared action and its result. Let a distinctive modular or relational graphic idea carry across the symbol, page composition and interaction card. Be visually inventive while remaining precise and scalable. Choose your own expressive palette and typography.
